body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. Saturday, October 3, 2026, and the day's top story is a pair of police chases that kept officers moving before dawn — one ending in a crash on South Union Avenue and a foot search through backyards. It's 73 degrees at Meadows Field right now, headed for a high near 100, with no active weather alerts for Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

Two police chases kept officers busy before dawn, one of them ending in a crash on South Union Avenue and a foot search through backyards, and a stabbing sent deputies to Oildale's Linda Vista area. A carnival drew a run of missing-child calls and a fight, crews handled vehicle fires on the southwest side, and a man was reported throwing knives and striking a relative with a bat at a home on Oregon Street. The rest of the log was medical aids, alarms and traffic checks.

Just after midnight a silver sedan reported at about 80 mph on southbound Highway 99 led officers onto city streets. The driver turned south on South H Street, went east on McKee Road and hit a dead end just east of Highway 99, made a U-turn, then crashed into the median on South Union Avenue near the 7500 block. He ran west along a fence line into a residential block near Acoma Way, and a sheriff's air unit followed him over backyards near Lazy River Drive before losing sight of him behind a home. Officers set a perimeter and worked through the yards.

At 12:38 a.m. a traffic stop on westbound Niles Street turned into a chase when a vehicle reported to be carrying at least five people took off. It ran east on Pioneer Drive through a red light at Fairfax Road, turned north on Meadows, and ended near the 4900 block of Pioneer Drive, where the occupants jumped a fence and ran. Officers detained three people and reported one still outstanding.

At 11:27 p.m. officers were sent to an apartment on the 3900 block of Oregon Street after a caller reported her brother was having a mental breakdown, was throwing knives around, and had hit another relative with a baseball bat. A verbal argument could be heard in the background and the call drew a heavy police and fire response. At 9:06 p.m. deputies were sent to the Linda Vista area for a stabbing; the caller reported a man had stab wounds to his arm and that the man's girlfriend was with him, and a suspect was reported leaving in a white Chevrolet Silverado.

Through the evening a carnival drew a run of missing-child reports. A 3-year-old girl in a Dodgers jersey was reported missing and found at the main gate, a 9-year-old boy was missing for about 15 minutes before he was located, a 2-year-old was reported missing before being found, and an 8-year-old girl was reported missing later in the night. Officers also handled a fight between two groups of women at the Ferris wheel. Crews were sent to a report of multiple vehicles burning at Playfair Road and Ashe Road around 9:35 p.m., and employees and security reported a man attempted to take merchandise in the Chester Avenue area just after 10 p.m.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 100° and a low around 71° tonight. It's currently 73° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. We don't have an air quality reading or active fire information to pass along this morning, so if you're headed out for yard work or a long walk, plan around the heat and check conditions before you go. Triple digits in October are nothing new here, but they still ask something of you — water, shade, and a little patience with the afternoon.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield Now reports that Bakersfield police are searching for a man who allegedly broke into Howard's Mini Mart through the roof.** That's the account from the department's own release, and it's the kind of detail that sticks with you — a break-in from above rather than through a door or window. Investigators are asking the public to keep an eye out as they work to identify him.

**According to 23ABC, the victims of the deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island have been identified.** REACH Air Medical Services says pilot Steven "Steve" Robinson and flight nurse Jessica deVries died when a medical helicopter went down in the Catalina waters shortly after takeoff on Sept. 30. The flight was carrying a patient, Catalina Hernandez, to the mainland for emergency care; her body was recovered after she had gone missing. Another flight nurse, Brad Sparks, continues his recovery, and Hernandez's son, who was on the flight, survived. Pacific Region President Sean Russell said the tragedy "has touched every corner of our organization."

**KGET 17 reports that a man faces life in prison after killing his wife, in a case where loved ones remembered that "they were all here every day."** The story centers on a family's loss and the sentence now hanging over the man convicted in it — a reminder of how much weight a courtroom carries for the people left behind.

**KGET 17 also reports that two Garces football stars are ineligible for Friday's game, with the status of the team's wins still up in the air.** For a program and a fan base that follow every snap, that leaves real questions about the season's record and what comes next. We'll be watching for the eligibility decision to sort itself out.

**23ABC spoke with criminal law attorney Jared Thompson about what California would require in a case like the one drawing national attention at Cornell University.** A former Cornell student says she was drugged and sexually assaulted by fraternity members in 2024; the men accused deny wrongdoing, no criminal charges have been filed, and New York Attorney General Letitia James has been appointed special prosecutor as the case returns to criminal review. Thompson explained that California's threshold goes well beyond whether someone had been drinking — prosecutors must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that a person was so intoxicated they didn't understand the nature of the act or its consequences, and that the accused knew or reasonably should have known the other party could not consent. California does not require a survivor to have been unconscious or physically unable to speak.

**KGET 17 reports that prosecutor Pedro Naveiras is making public safety the centerpiece of his bid for Bakersfield's third ward.** It's a city council race where the pitch is straightforward: a career prosecutor arguing that his courtroom experience is what the ward needs. Voters in the third ward will weigh that against whatever their own priorities are when ballots arrive.

**23ABC reports that Seth Griffith is back for his seventh season with the Bakersfield Condors, still chasing a Calder Cup.** The captain has worn the "C," helped bring younger players along, and watched teammates graduate to the Edmonton Oilers — but the one box unchecked is a championship. "I haven't won a Calder Cup," Griffith said, pointing to how much fun the Marlies had celebrating last year. He talks about running the room like an NHL dressing room and making sure every player understands his role, which matters in the AHL, where call-ups and injuries churned through nearly 40 players last season. The Condors open the 2026-27 season this weekend in Henderson, Nevada, with four straight road games to start.

## Something good

Seth Griffith's seventh season in Condorstown is worth a smile on its own. A captain who keeps showing up, keeps teaching, and keeps chasing the one trophy that's eluded him gives local hockey fans another winter of professional hockey to look forward to — and gives the younger guys in that locker room someone to learn from. Here's hoping this is the year.

## Coming up this week

The week ahead is busy on the civic side. The Special Youth Commission meets this morning, Saturday, October 3, at 9:00 a.m. The Youth Commission holds its regular meeting Monday, October 5, at 4:30 p.m. Wednesday, October 7, is the heavy day: the Police Civil Service Commission meets at 8:30 a.m., City Council Meeting 330 convenes at 3:30 p.m., and City Council Meeting 515 follows at 5:15 p.m. Then Thursday, October 8, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon, and Friday, October 9, the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets at noon. If you've got a question about housing, neighborhood safety, or city business, this is the week to show up and be heard.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. "Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein" screens Monday, October 5. NB RIDAZ brings the "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour" to the Fox on Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." lands Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour takes the stage Saturday, October 17. The Fox's Cults & Classics season pass for 2026-2027 is also on sale now if you'd rather plan the whole year at once.

Have a good Saturday, Bakersfield. Drink water, check on your neighbors, and we'll see you tomorrow.

top.title: BPD: Search for man who allegedly broke into Howard’s Mini Mart through the roof
